reasons.reason: When alpha plus beta equals one, the recursion still pulls conditional variance back toward a long-run level after each spike, and that pull back after shocks is exactly what mean-reverting volatility describes.
Setting alpha plus beta to exactly one puts a unit root in the conditional variance equation, so volatility shocks persist indefinitely, and that restricted case is what gets called integrated GARCH.
The Chow statistic compares restricted and unrestricted residual sums of squares and is F-distributed under no break, and by splitting the sample at several points you can flag more than one break.
The classic Chow test needs the break date chosen in advance, assumes equal error variance in both subsamples so the pooled F works, and under the null its statistic follows an F-distribution.

Stability means shocks die out over time, and that only happens when every eigenvalue of the companion matrix lies strictly inside the unit circle, so powers of the matrix shrink toward zero.

A stable system settles into a steady long-run relationship between capex and revenue, and that steady state corresponds to an eigenvalue of exactly one, which keeps the levels from exploding or collapsing.
A zero-one dummy entered on its own shifts the whole cost line up or down after the regulation while leaving its slope alone, so its coefficient measures the change in the intercept.

Regulatory changes mostly affect how unpredictable costs become once they take effect, so the dummy's coefficient captures how much the spread of the cost function differs between the before and after periods.
